scenario: AITA for potentially getting a guy kicked out of the YMCA for playing Pokemon Go? | I (F18) work at a food place that’s placed inside a YMCA. Its in the middle of a long hallway that leads to four hockey arenas and is secluded from the more popular areas of the Y such as the gym. it’s summer, no people except the staff of the Y that aren’t near where my work is. Days are slow therefore I’m booked to work alone. Last saturday I had a shift, and no one was there except the casual gym nuts that ordering from my store. One man, mid 30s was one of my customers that day. I didn’t make much of it at first, he ordered some food from me and then that was that, a normal customer transaction. However, i noticed how he walked back and forth every few minutes in the hallway between my store and the arenas that lead to the gym. I really didn’t care at this point, and went onto minding my business. He continues to do so for three hours of my shift and I start freaking out, but i end up not doing anything except panic silently until the next person takes my shift. Monday rolls by and I had a closing shift alone. 3 hours left of my shift the same guy comes back. He bought more food and this time i asked if he worked in the facility, and replied “no, i’m just visiting.” I felt uneasy about the whole interaction given what happened, but he left with his food right away and i took a breath of relief. However, 30 minutes later I see him once more pace the same path he took saturday, this time looking at his phone then into the store and everytime He does this for another 2 hours and I continue to do my usual work routine, but now with shaky hands, avoiding eye contact with this creep. I don’t deal really well with confrontations due to my anxiety so i quietly suffered in my nervous sweat alone. Thankfully my parents came to visit knowing I had a night shift. told them what was going on and was going on and was comforted. Since I had to start closing my mom went to go get the security for me to talk to, and dad stood guard while i cleaned the store. the staff gave me phone numbers and said they’d escort me if ever I felt unsafe. They also said that they’ve checked the cameras and even got the guy’s face and the next time he does this will be kicked out, doesn’t matter if its me who saw. The staff and I never confronted the guy but he continued to pace back and forth while i was talking to the staff and he ended up leaving since the place was closing for the night. Once home, my dad told me that everytime the guy passed by he would give him the dirty look while we were talking to the YMCA staff. The man then told my dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go and even showed him his phone. I now feel like an asshole if this were to be true, but doesn’t stop the fact that if he really was just playing a game, the next time he’s going to do it he’ll face be kicked out of the YMCA. AITA?

Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

So, there's this person, let's call her Alice, who works at a food place inside a YMCA. It's a pretty secluded area, not near the main gym or popular spots. On a Saturday, she had a slow shift and was working alone. A man in his mid-30s came in, bought some food, and then started pacing back and forth in the hallway between her store and the hockey arenas. She didn't think much of it at first, but after three hours of this, she started to feel uneasy and panicky. She didn't do anything except panic silently until her shift ended.

Then, on Monday, she had another shift, again alone. Three hours into her shift, the same man came back, bought more food, and when she asked if he worked there, he said he was just visiting. She felt uneasy again, but he left quickly. However, 30 minutes later, he came back and started pacing the same hallway, looking at his phone and into the store. This went on for another two hours, and Alice was really anxious, shaking and avoiding eye contact. She has anxiety and doesn't handle confrontations well, so she just suffered in silence.

Her parents came to visit that night, knowing she had a night shift. She told them what was happening, and they comforted her. Her mom went to get security to talk to, and her dad stood guard while she cleaned the store. The staff gave her phone numbers and said they'd escort her if she ever felt unsafe. They also mentioned they checked the cameras and got the guy's face, so the next time he does this, he'll be kicked out, regardless of whether Alice saw him.

The staff and Alice never confronted the guy, but he continued pacing back and forth while they were talking to the staff. He ended up leaving since the place was closing for the night. Once home, her dad told her that every time the guy passed by, he gave him the dirty look while they were talking to the YMCA staff. The man then told her dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go and even showed him his phone. Now, Alice feels like an asshole if this were true, but she still thinks that if he was really just playing a game, the next time he does it, he'll be kicked out of the YMCA. She's asking if she's AITA (Am I The Asshole).

Alright, so the question is whether her actions are morally acceptable. Let me break this down.

First, Alice felt uneasy about the man pacing back and forth for hours. She didn't confront him because of her anxiety and fear of confrontation. Instead, she told her parents, who then got security involved. The staff checked the cameras, identified the man, and decided to kick him out the next time he does this.

The man later told her dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go and showed his phone. So, it seems like he wasn't up to any malicious activity; he was just playing a game while pacing.

Now, Alice feels bad because maybe she overreacted, but she still thinks that if he was just playing a game, he should be kicked out next time.

So, is her action of getting security involved and potentially having the man kicked out for playing Pokemon Go morally acceptable?

I think the key points here are:

1. Alice felt unsafe because of the man's behavior. She was working alone in a secluded area, and the man was pacing back and forth for hours. This made her anxious and uncomfortable.

2. She didn't confront him directly because of her anxiety, but she did tell her parents, who then involved security.

3. The staff checked the cameras, identified the man, and decided to take action against him.

4. The man later claimed he was just playing Pokemon Go and showed his phone as proof.

So, from Alice's perspective, she felt threatened and took steps to ensure her safety. She didn't confront the man herself but involved her parents and the staff, who then took appropriate measures.

However, the man's explanation that he was just playing Pokemon Go complicates things. If he was indeed just playing a game, then his behavior might not have been threatening, and Alice's reaction might have been an overreaction.

But, on the other hand, Alice's feelings of unease and anxiety are valid. She had a right to feel unsafe and to take steps to protect herself.

So, is it morally acceptable for her to involve security and potentially have the man kicked out for what might have been a harmless activity?

I think it depends on whether her actions were reasonable given her feelings of safety and whether the staff's decision to kick him out was based on her report and the man's behavior.

If the man was just playing Pokemon Go and wasn't causing any harm, then perhaps Alice's actions were a bit harsh. However, if his pacing and presence made her feel unsafe, then her actions were justified to ensure her safety.

Additionally, the staff checked the cameras and identified him, so they had evidence of his behavior. They decided to take action, which might have been a bit extreme, but it was their decision based on the situation.

In the end, Alice's main concern was her safety, and she took steps to address it. Even if the man was just playing a game, her feelings of unease were legitimate, and she had the right to feel safe at work.

Therefore, I think her actions were morally acceptable because she prioritized her safety and took appropriate steps to address her concerns.
